elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the amounts paid or payable by Sanofi ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim." The cap runs to "each Party", so it is symmetrical in application even though the measure is Customer-side payments (the standard mutual construction).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is a single measure — "the amounts paid or payable by Sanofi ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — with no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "greater of" construction; it also uses the broader noun "amounts" rather than "fees". To reach preferred, the drafter must render "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained first sentence: "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS..." — bilateral by its terms and left unchanged.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained carve-out: "NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT ... DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER ARTICLE XI", and the new cap sentence opens "Subject to the foregoing", so the cap does not reach confidentiality damages.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out sentence names only indemnification (14.1/14.2), confidentiality (Article XI) and intellectual property (Article X); no data protection or security obligations are excepted, and the new sentence excepts only gross negligence and willful misconduct. A separate "data protection and security obligations" carve-out would have to be added.

"NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE INDEMNIFICATION RIGHTS OR OBLIGATIONS OF ANY PARTY UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR SECTION 14.2"; the inserted cap sits inside Section 14.5 and is expressly "Subject to the foregoing", so indemnities sit outside the cap.

Inserted language: "except in the case of a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, each Party's aggregate liability ... shall not exceed..." — gross negligence is expressly outside the cap for both parties.
Same inserted exception: "except in the case of a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
Neither the retained carve-out sentence nor the inserted exception mentions fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; fraud would fall within the new monetary cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The retained carve-out preserves "DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO ... INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY UNDER ARTICLE X". Whether Article X's obligations encompass infringement of the other Party's IP cannot be confirmed because Article X is not supplied; the wording is breach-of-obligation based rather than infringement based.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language states that Sanofi's obligation to pay amounts due under the Agreement is not "damages" subject to the cap; as drafted the cap could be argued to limit recovery of unpaid amounts. A short sentence excluding Customer payment obligations from the cap is required.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — applies to both Parties; no residual language leaves Customer uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the amounts paid or payable by Sanofi under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a Customer-payment, twelve-month basis. "Amounts" is broader than "fees" (noted in the rationale for preferred), but it remains a 12-month payments basis and is not less favourable to Customer.

Retained: "NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 ... SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE INDEMNIFICATION RIGHTS OR OBLIGATIONS OF ANY PARTY UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR SECTION 14.2", and the new cap is "Subject to the foregoing".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained: "... OR DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER ARTICLE XI", preserved by the "Subject to the foregoing" opener of the new cap.
"except in the case of a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct" in the inserted cap sentence.
Same inserted exception covers willful misconduct for both Parties.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all six fallback elements are met in operative language — a mutual "each Party's aggregate liability" cap on a twelve-month Customer-payment basis, with indemnification and confidentiality preserved outside the cap by the retained carve-out sentence (imported into the new sentence via "Subject to the foregoing") and gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly excepted.

Preferred is not met: no USD 1,000,000 floor / "greater of" construction, no data protection and security carve-out, no fraud carve-out, no Customer-payment-obligations exclusion, and the IP carve-out is expressed as breach of Article X obligations rather than infringement of the other party's IP (Article X not supplied).

Minimality holds: a single sentence was inserted, nothing was deleted or paraphrased, the existing mutual consequential-damages waiver and carve-out sentence are retained verbatim, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, additional damages categories, USD floor) were added beyond the fallback checklist.

Intent preserved: the "Subject to the foregoing" opener prevents any contradiction with the retained "NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 ... SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT" sentence; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced (Sections 14.1/14.2, Articles X and XI remain intact), and Section 14.6 and Section 15.6(a) are untouched.

Drafting notes if the counterparty pushes back or if we want to move toward preferred: (i) change "amounts paid or payable by Sanofi" to "fees paid or payable by Sanofi" and anchor to "the event giving rise to the claim"; (ii) add "the greater of ... and USD 1,000,000"; (iii) add data protection/security and fraud to the carve-outs; (iv) add a sentence confirming Sanofi's obligation to pay amounts due is not subject to the cap.
